description: Implement the T1-T5 autonomy spec as a set of coherent, data-shape-first behavioral changes to the decision pipeline, using TDD (write failing tests first, then implement). The pieces: T2 raise the default escalation gate from 0.6 to 0.85 (keep the OR semantics: escalate when operationConfidence < 0.85 OR targetConfidence < 0.85); T4 (the key change) make escalation never kill autonomy - when the client LLM is unreachable (no sampling capability, or the sampling request throws/times out) the step must fall back to Laya's best guess with op != BLOCKED and a warning note so the run continues, with only Laya itself choosing BLOCKED, the loop detector, or the destructive guard able to stop a run; T5 record per-step inference milliseconds on the StepRecord and surface a run-level autonomy summary (% fully autonomous = rule+laya steps / total). T1 (rules carry conf 0.97, LLM never in the default path) and T3 (escalation scoped to exactly one step, autonomous resume) are ALREADY satisfied by the current code - verify them and add regression tests that would fail if the behavior regressed. Design the boundary changes first (config default, escalation signature/EscalationResult, StepRecord shape) before editing the loop; keep src/types.ts pure and config parsed once. Do the work as a single coherent unit but batch the edits by concern; these changes are interdependent so they must land together.
steps: DESIGN FIRST (no behavior yet): decide the boundary changes. (a) config.ts: DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD constant 0.6 -> 0.85 and update the doc-comment block near the top that documents LAYA_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.6. (b) escalation.ts: extend escalate() so the caller can pass Laya's original (pre-escalation) decision as a fallback, e.g. add an optional `fallback?: Decision` to EscalationOptions (or a dedicated param). When `sample` is undefined OR the sampler throws/times out, escalate must return that fallback decision (only when its operation != BLOCKED) with escalated:false and a clear warning note, instead of the current hard BLOCKED. When no usable non-BLOCKED fallback exists, preserve the existing graceful BLOCKED. Keep the parseDecision path unchanged. (c) loop.ts StepRecord: add an optional `inferenceMs?: number` field (per-step wall time for the decision, i.e. the engine.decide / escalate call), documented as observational. (d) A run-level autonomy summary shape (e.g. an `autonomy` field on RunResult: { total, rule, laya, llm, stub, fullyAutonomous, autonomousPct }) - keep RunResult additive/optional so existing tests do not break.

T2 - failing test first: in test/autopilot.test.ts or test/config.test.ts (config.test.ts already asserts the default threshold) update/add a test asserting loadConfig().confidenceThreshold === 0.85 by default and that LAYA_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD env still overrides. Then change DEFAULT_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD to 0.85 in src/config.ts and fix the doc comment. Search the repo for any test that hard-codes 0.6 as the expected default (grep for '0.6' in test/) and update those expectations; do NOT change tests that pass confidenceThreshold: 0.6 explicitly as an argument (those are intentional per-call overrides).

T4 - failing tests first (behavior, not implementation): add tests (extend test/escalation.test.ts for the unit boundary and test/autopilot-autonomy.test.ts for the loop behavior) that assert: (i) escalate() with sample=undefined and a non-BLOCKED Laya fallback returns that fallback (op != BLOCKED), escalated:false, with a warning note; (ii) escalate() with a sampler that throws returns the fallback likewise; (iii) in runGoal, when the local Laya engine returns a LOW-confidence but non-BLOCKED decision (e.g. CLICK with opConf 0.5) and NO sampler is wired (client lacks sampling), the run does NOT end BLOCKED on that step - it executes Laya's best guess and continues, and the transcript step carries source 'laya' with a warning note; (iv) a run only stops for BLOCKED when Laya itself chose BLOCKED, or via the existing loop detector / destructive guard. Then implement: in the loop's confidence-check block, pass the current (Laya/rule-refined) decision into escalate as the fallback so an unreachable LLM degrades to Laya's guess instead of BLOCKED. Preserve the existing behavior when the sampler IS present and returns a usable decision (source 'llm').

T3 - regression test: add a test in test/autopilot-autonomy.test.ts (or a new test/autopilot-escalation-scope.test.ts) proving escalation is scoped to exactly one step: drive a run where step N escalates to the LLM (low-confidence Laya + a sampler) and step N+1 is decided again by rules/Laya (source 'rule' or 'laya', NOT 'llm'), and the run does not end merely because one step escalated. This should PASS against the current code (the loop recomputes the decision each iteration); if it fails, fix the loop so no latched 'LLM mode' exists.

T1 - regression test: add/confirm a test asserting rule-seeded decisions carry operationConfidence 0.97 (RULE_CONFIDENCE) and that on a step a rule can decide, no sampler call is made (the LLM is never in the default path). policy.ts already sets RULE_CONFIDENCE=0.97; the test guards against regression.

T5 - inference timing + autonomy summary: in runGoal, wrap the decision computation (policySeed + engine.decide + escalate) with a wall-clock measurement and set record.inferenceMs on each StepRecord. Compute the run-level autonomy summary after the loop (count steps by source; fullyAutonomous = steps whose source is 'rule' or 'laya' or 'stub'; autonomousPct = fullyAutonomous/total) and attach it to RunResult additively. Surface it in src/tools/run_goal.ts renderRunResult (a compact line like 'Autonomy: 4/5 steps local (80%); inference: median NN ms' and per-step 'inf=NNms' in the transcript line). Add a test asserting the summary math and that inferenceMs is present and finite on executed steps.

Run `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run build`, and the full `pnpm test` suite. Fix any fallout in other tests caused by the threshold change or the additive RunResult field. Keep the offline suite fully green with the StubEngine and no weights.
acceptance_criteria: loadConfig().confidenceThreshold defaults to 0.85; LAYA_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD still overrides; OR escalation semantics preserved (escalate when opConf<0.85 OR tgtConf<0.85).

escalate() returns Laya's non-BLOCKED fallback (escalated:false, with a warning note) when the sampler is undefined or throws; it still returns a usable LLM decision when the sampler answers, and still returns graceful BLOCKED only when there is no non-BLOCKED fallback.

In runGoal, a low-confidence non-BLOCKED Laya decision with no reachable LLM executes Laya's best guess and the run continues (not BLOCKED); a run stops for BLOCKED only when Laya itself chose BLOCKED, or via the loop detector / destructive guard.
A regression test proves escalation is scoped to one step and the next step returns to rules/Laya (no latched LLM mode) and does not end the run.
Rule-seeded decisions carry confidence 0.97 and no sampler is consulted on a rule-decided step.
Each executed StepRecord carries a finite inferenceMs, and RunResult carries an autonomy summary (fullyAutonomous count + autonomousPct) surfaced by renderRunResult.
`pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run build`, and `pnpm test` all pass; the offline suite is green with the stub and no weights.
src/types.ts remains pure (no playwright/onnx imports) and config is still parsed once in src/config.ts.
verification: pnpm exec vitest run test/escalation.test.ts test/autopilot-autonomy.test.ts test/config.test.ts
